subject: Discovery recap — buying route & approval ladder
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Emily Carter <emily@brightleaf.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@brightleaf.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap — buying route & approval ladder

Hi Emily / Alex / Procurement team,

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and the outstanding items I promised to surface for internal alignment at BrightLeaf: 

1) Two likely purchase routes we discussed
   - Card (Procurement bypass): Small annual commitment paid by credit card for initial POC (<= $25k). Fastest procurement (~1-2 weeks).
   - PO / Contract: For enterprise rollout, requires SOW + PO, finance signoff, and legal review (expected 4–8 weeks).

2) Marketplace option
   - You mentioned AWS Marketplace as a preference for centralized procurement. If BrightLeaf buys via marketplace, invoicing and entitlements are handled by AWS and our contract is simplified (no DocuSign required on your side), but subscription billing will be via AWS terms.

3) Budget/approval ladder (what we need to confirm)
   - Economic buyer: likely Emily Carter (Head of AI) — controls $ for pilot and expansion.
   - Finance sponsor: Alex Rios (Budget owner in Finance Ops) — will sign PO and route to Accounts Payable.
   - Legal/Compliance: procurement@brightleaf.com will handle standard IP/data clauses and any SOC2 addenda.

Next steps I propose:
- Emily: confirm which purchase route you want to pursue for the pilot (card vs PO vs marketplace).
- Procurement: confirm required PO template fields and routing contacts (billing contact, AP email, any PO number formatting).
- Diego / Marissa / Sergio (Redwood): we will prepare a short SOW + pricing summary and a marketplace SKU mapping if you want the AWS route.

I attached a very short "approval ladder" sketch (MAP-approval-ladder_v1.pdf) and a draft SOW. I also dropped the pricing summary for quick budget checks.

Available this week for a 20-min follow-up if helpful — I can loop in our finance ops engineer (Sergio) to answer PO/marketplace integration questions.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0123

Attachments: MAP-approval-ladder_v1.pdf (1 page), SOW-draft_BrightLeaf.docx (2 pages), pricing-summary.csv

From: Emily Carter <emily@brightleaf.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@brightleaf.com>, Alex Rios <alex.rios@brightleaf.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T12:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — buying route & approval ladder

Diego — thanks for the recap and the docs. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- For the pilot (3-month, ~10k token volume estimate) we prefer the card route to avoid involving Legal for the moment. If the pilot shows signal we will go PO for annual.
- We are interested in AWS Marketplace but need to confirm whether procurement will allow it for a pilot; procurement typically prefers a PO but will approve marketplace if the vendor is already in our vendor registry.

Alex (cc'd) — can you confirm:
1) If procurement will accept an AWS Marketplace subscription for a pilot?
2) If not, can we do a one-time P-card transaction — what approvals are required?

Also — budget holder for this initiative is indeed me, but AP signatory is Alex. I'll share this email with our vendor-onboarding team after we confirm the route.

— Emily
Head of AI | BrightLeaf Health

From: Alex Rios <alex.rios@brightleaf.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Emily Carter <emily@brightleaf.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@brightleaf.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — buying route & approval ladder

Diego / Emily — quick from Finance / Procurement POV: 

- Marketplace: acceptable, but only if Redwood is listed on AWS Marketplace and we can get a consolidated invoice under our Master Contract. Our vendor onboarding requires an existing marketplace SKU and Merchant of Record to be verified. Expect ~3 business days to check registry.
- P-card (procurement card): allowed for purchases under $25k but requires my approval + AP coding. For anything above $25k, we need a PO.
- PO path: please provide a short SOW and a standard commercial attachment (term sheet). We'll route PO to me (Finance Ops) then Legal if terms deviate from our template.

From Procurement: the PO needs the following fields: vendor legal name, tax ID, remit-to address, payment terms (Net 30), and quote reference. If Redwood provides a marketplace SKU we can skip vendor onboarding but still need the internal PO for allocation.

I will confirm by EOD whether Marketplace is available for the pilot. If not, Emily — we should sign off on the P-card route so we can start next week.

Thanks,
Alex Rios
Finance Operations Manager | BrightLeaf Health

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Emily Carter <emily@brightleaf.com>, Alex Rios <alex.rios@brightleaf.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@brightleaf.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-13T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — buying route & approval ladder

Emily / Alex / Procurement — great, thanks for the quick clarifications. Short follow-up and proposed plan: 

1) Pilot route decision (choose one this week)
   - Option A — Card: Redwood will generate a one-time invoice/checkout link for ~$12k (3-month pilot). Fastest start.
   - Option B — AWS Marketplace: Redwood will map the pilot to SKU RL-ML-STD-100 and provide the marketplace listing URL; BrightLeaf confirms merchant-of-record acceptance and we proceed via AWS billing.
   - Option C — PO: Redwood prepares a one-page SOW + quotation; BrightLeaf issues PO referencing the quote number and we start upon PO date.

2) What we need from BrightLeaf to proceed quickly
   - If Card: Emily approves and Alex confirms P-card sign-off.
   - If Marketplace: Procurement confirms vendor SKU acceptance and AP provides the internal charge code.
   - If PO: Procurement sends PO template and preferred billing contact; Diego to deliver SOW and commercial attachment by EOD tomorrow.

3) Internal approval ladder (explicit mapping from our side)
   - Economic buyer: Emily Carter — approves budget and pilot metrics.
   - Finance sponsor / AP signatory: Alex Rios — approves P-card or signs PO.
   - Procurement contact: procurement@brightleaf.com — vendor onboarding & compliance.
   - Legal review: only if PO terms deviate from BrightLeaf standard; otherwise Legal triage not required for pilot.

Action items (owner / due):
- Diego: update SOW to include explicit success criteria and send final pricing CSV (Due: 2026-10-14 EOD).
- Alex: confirm marketplace acceptance or P-card approval (Due: 2026-10-13 EOD).
- Emily: confirm pilot route (Due: 2026-10-13 EOD).

I'll attach a cleaned-up approval ladder and a one-page SOW (see attachments). If it's helpful, Marissa (cc) and I can run a short 15-min call with Alex to walk through the PO fields so AP can author the PO quickly.

Best,
Diego
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
